title: Esther Bible Quiz - Chapter 7
description: Ten questions on Esther 7: Esther's second banquet, where she names Haman as the enemy and he is hanged on his own gallows.

questions.text: Who came to the banquet with Esther the queen?
questions.explanation: The king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.

questions.text: How far did the king say he would go to grant Esther's request?
questions.explanation: The king told Esther that even to the half of the kingdom her request would be performed.

answers.text: Even to half of the kingdom

questions.text: What did Esther ask to be given to her at her petition and request?
questions.explanation: Esther asked that her life be given her at her petition, and her people at her request.

questions.text: Esther said she would have held her peace if they had only been sold as what?
questions.explanation: Esther said that if they had been sold for male and female slaves, she would have held her peace.

questions.text: Whom did Esther name as the adversary and enemy?
questions.explanation: Esther said the adversary and enemy was "this wicked Haman".

questions.text: Where did the king go when he arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine?
questions.explanation: The king arose in his wrath and went into the palace garden.

questions.text: Why did Haman stand up after the king left the banquet?
questions.explanation: Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen, because he saw that evil was determined against him.

answers.text: To accuse Mordecai before the king
To plead with Esther for his life

questions.text: When the king came back from the garden, where had Haman fallen?
questions.explanation: When the king returned, Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was.

answers.text: On the couch where Esther was
Into a pool in the garden

questions.text: Who told the king about the gallows that Haman had made for Mordecai?
questions.explanation: Harbonah, one of the eunuchs who were with the king, spoke of the gallows fifty cubits high standing at Haman's house.

questions.text: What happened to the king's wrath after Haman was hanged?
questions.explanation: After Haman was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, the king's wrath was pacified.
